title: Grade 8 Science — Thu, Jun 19
description: Coal and Petroleum — Day 4 of 5: CNG vs LPG; non-renewable fuels; conservation; PCRA
subject: science

questions.question: CNG stands for:
questions.explanation: CNG = Compressed Natural Gas. It is natural gas (mainly methane) stored at high pressure and used as fuel for vehicles.

questions.question: LPG is mainly composed of:
questions.explanation: LPG (Liquefied Petroleum Gas) consists mainly of propane (C₃H₈) and butane (C₄H₁₀), liquefied under pressure for storage in cylinders.

questions.question: CNG is considered an environment-friendly fuel for vehicles because:
options: It burns more completely and produces fewer pollutants than petrol or diesel
questions.explanation: CNG burns cleaner than petrol or diesel, producing less CO₂, almost no SO₂, and negligible particulate matter — making it more environment-friendly.

questions.question: Which fuel is used for cooking in Indian household cylinders?
questions.explanation: LPG (Liquefied Petroleum Gas) in pressurised cylinders is the standard cooking fuel in Indian homes.

questions.question: Natural gas is found:
options: Above petroleum deposits (lighter, rises to the top)
questions.explanation: Natural gas (being lighter than petroleum) collects above crude oil deposits. It is often found at the top of oil wells.

questions.question: Why are coal and petroleum called non-renewable resources?
options: They take millions of years to form and cannot be replenished once used up
They cannot be found in India
They are only found in solid form
questions.explanation: Non-renewable resources are those that took millions of years to form. Once depleted, they cannot be replaced in any practical timeframe.

questions.question: PCRA stands for:
questions.explanation: PCRA = Petroleum Conservation Research Association. It is an Indian government agency that promotes fuel conservation and efficient use of petroleum products.

questions.question: Which of the following is a fuel conservation tip recommended by PCRA?
options: Keep the vehicle engine running at red lights
Keep tyres properly inflated and service vehicles regularly
Use older vehicles that consume more fuel
questions.explanation: Properly inflated tyres and regular servicing improve fuel efficiency. PCRA recommends these along with switching off engines at long red lights.

questions.question: CNG vehicles emit much less of which harmful gas compared to petrol vehicles?
questions.explanation: CNG vehicles emit far less sulphur dioxide (SO₂) and particulate matter compared to petrol or diesel vehicles, greatly reducing smog and lung diseases.

questions.question: The gas added to LPG cylinders to detect gas leaks by smell is called:
questions.explanation: Ethyl mercaptan (ethane thiol) is added to odourless LPG to give it a distinctive unpleasant smell, helping detect leaks and prevent accidents.

questions.question: If petroleum resources run out, the most likely impact on modern life would be:
options: Severe disruption — transport, plastics, electricity generation, and industries all depend on petroleum
Nothing major — alternatives are already available
questions.explanation: Modern civilization is heavily dependent on petroleum for transport fuels, plastics, medicines, synthetic fibres, and electricity. Its depletion would cause severe disruption.

questions.question: Which renewable energy alternative can reduce dependence on fossil fuels?
questions.explanation: Solar, wind, hydroelectric, and tidal energy are renewable alternatives that can reduce dependence on finite, polluting fossil fuels.

questions.question: Which is the CORRECT comparison between CNG and LPG?
options: CNG is used in cooking; LPG is used in vehicles
CNG is mainly methane (gas); LPG is mainly propane/butane (liquid under pressure)
LPG is more environment-friendly than CNG
questions.explanation: CNG = compressed methane (vehicle fuel); LPG = liquefied propane/butane (cooking fuel). Both are cleaner than petrol/diesel but differ in composition and use.

questions.question: Natural gas is used as a fuel in:
options: Power plants, industries, homes, and vehicles (CNG/PNG)
questions.explanation: Natural gas has versatile uses: power generation, industrial processes, cooking (PNG — Piped Natural Gas), and as CNG for vehicles.

questions.question: Why should we conserve petroleum products?
options: Because they are non-renewable, finite, and polluting — conserving them extends supplies and reduces environmental harm
Because the government has ordered it
Because they are only found abroad
questions.explanation: Conservation is essential because petroleum is non-renewable (will run out), polluting (CO₂, SO₂), and has many other non-fuel uses (plastics, medicines) that make it too valuable to burn wastefully.
